headline: Medium prompt-injection and data-leakage risks arise from shared document workflows; Perplexity’s vendor-hosted browsing can amplify downstream errors.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: PaddleOCR ingests documents/images and Perplexity ingests uploaded documents and browsing context. If PaddleOCR output is passed into Perplexity without sanitization, attacker-controlled text in documents can be reinterpreted as instructions. This is a plausible default workflow, not a provably blocked one.
conditions: IF PaddleOCR output is copied into Perplexity prompts or uploads
IF the source document contains instruction-like text
mitigations: Strip instructions from OCR output before reuse
Use a fixed prompt template that quotes OCR text verbatim
Mark OCR text as untrusted in the workflow
Review a sample of outputs for instruction-following behavior

B_data_leakage.rationale: PaddleOCR touches documents and images, while Perplexity accepts uploaded PDFs/images and sends queries to vendor APIs/search providers. A shared document workflow can move sensitive content from A into B’s hosted backend, creating a realistic leakage path in default use.
conditions: IF documents or images processed by PaddleOCR are uploaded to Perplexity
IF those files contain sensitive or regulated data
mitigations: Redact sensitive fields before upload
Use synthetic test documents for validation
Disable upload of confidential files in the workflow
Limit Perplexity use to non-sensitive summaries

C_capability_conflict.rationale: PaddleOCR has allowlisted network egress and browser capability, while Perplexity has vendor-only egress and no filesystem write or shell. Their write surfaces do not overlap, so direct resource conflict is limited; the main overlap is read/analysis, not mutable state.
conditions: IF both agents are forced to modify the same external resource through a separate orchestrator
mitigations: Keep each agent on separate work queues
Avoid shared mutable folders
Serialize any external writes through one controller
Use read-only handoff files

D_cascading_error.rationale: Perplexity is a search-RAG system with live web search and citations, so it may treat PaddleOCR-derived text as input for multi-hop reasoning. If OCR errors or hallucinated extractions are forwarded without verification, Perplexity can amplify them into polished but wrong answers or actions.
conditions: IF Perplexity is instructed to trust PaddleOCR output as authoritative
IF no human or programmatic verification step checks OCR accuracy
mitigations: Require confidence thresholds before forwarding OCR text
Compare OCR output against the source image for key fields
Add a verification step before any downstream action
Annotate OCR-derived facts as provisional

E_compliance.rationale: PaddleOCR processes documents and images, and Perplexity uploads documents to a vendor-hosted service with browsing context and API calls. If regulated data such as EU PII or confidential documents are routed from A into B, retention and residency obligations may diverge; the profiles do not show a shared compliance regime, so uncertainty pushes upward.
conditions: IF regulated personal data is included in documents processed by PaddleOCR
IF those documents are uploaded into Perplexity
mitigations: Classify documents before routing them
Block regulated data from vendor-hosted analysis
Review Perplexity retention/privacy terms for the data class
Use local-only OCR for sensitive workloads
